column3: The Greek explicitly says the Pharisees “heard” and repeats the name Jesus in their report.
The Greek says He went away “again” into Galilee; BSB renders this as returning.
The Greek coordinates the well’s presence with Jesus’ sitting rather than explicitly making it causal with “Since.”
BSB renders Greek present “comes” and “says” as past.
BSB moves the statement that He is a Jew before the question and renders present “says” as past.
The Greek quotes “Give Me to drink” directly; BSB paraphrases it as asking for a drink.
The Greek asks where He “has” living water, rather than where He “will get” it.
The Greek connects the second clause with “but” rather than “Indeed.”
The Greek says she would not come here to draw; “have to keep” makes the necessity and repetition explicit.
“Jesus” supplies the unnamed subject; the Greek says “come here,” rather than specifically “come back.”
The Greek directly repeats her words “I have no husband”; BSB recasts them as “you have no husband.”
“Jews” makes the plural audience explicit; the Greek has “and” rather than “but.”
The Greek says the hour “is now,” rather than “has now come.”
The Greek says the disciples came, rather than explicitly returned. “From her” supplies an object of seeking.
